links.outcome: Whether physician review of AI-drafted patient messages caught and corrected embedded errors
links.effect: Each erroneous draft was missed by 13-15 of 20 PCPs; 35-45% submitted unedited; only one participant addressed all four errors; mean 2.67 of 4 missed.
links.quote: Each erroneous AI draft was “missed” by at least 13 participants (65%) and was submitted entirely unedited by at least seven participants (35%).

links.outcome: Automation complacency letting erroneous AI-drafted messages reach patients after physician review
links.effect: All but one physician sent at least one erroneous response; likelihood of a missed error significantly greater than zero (p<0.001) for each erroneous draft; 90% trusted the tool.
links.quote: In this simulated environment, all but one physician ‘sent’ at least one fictitious response to a patient that contained an error.

links.outcome: Whether physicians detected incorrect AI outputs (automation bias/overreliance)
links.effect: Physicians missed 65-75% of erroneous drafts (13-15 of 20); 90% agreed they trusted the AI tool and 75% believed drafts were safe to use.
links.quote: Participants missed an average of 2.67 out of four (66.6%) erroneous AI drafts.

links.outcome: Passive acceptance of flawed AI drafts in a standard editable draft interface
links.effect: With a standard editable draft interface, 35-45% of erroneous drafts were submitted entirely unedited and 65-75% were insufficiently corrected.
links.quote: Each erroneous AI draft was “missed” by at least 13 participants (65%) and was submitted entirely unedited by at least seven participants (35%).

links.outcome: AI drafts failing to escalate urgent conditions (blood clot, DKA) in patient messages
links.effect: AI drafts for blood clot risk and DKA risk omitted urgent escalation; these were missed by 13 (65%) and 15 (75%) physicians respectively.
links.quote: The AI draft does not address the risk of diabetic ketoacidosis which requires urgent intervention.

links.outcome: Harmful errors or delayed escalation in AI-drafted replies to symptom-related messages
links.effect: Two of four erroneous drafts were potentially harmful omissions (blood clot, DKA), which physicians missed in 65% and 75% of cases.
links.quote: These erroneous messages were then categorized via team consensus: two were identified as objective inaccuracies, and two were identified as potentially harmful omission (Table 3 ).

links.outcome: Outdated clinical knowledge and omission of serious diagnoses in AI drafts
links.effect: AI drafts contained outdated COVID vaccine timing advice and omitted DKA and blood clot urgency; 4 of 18 drafts (22%) erroneous.
links.quote: Four (22%) of these PPMs were identified as erroneous.
